subject: springboot
question: A @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) test is @Transactional and calls the API via TestRestTemplate. Why are the inserted rows not rolled back?
options: The server handles the request in a different thread and transaction
TestRestTemplate commits the test transaction
Rollback only works with JUnit 4
RANDOM_PORT disables all transactions
explanation: Test-managed rollback applies to the test thread's transaction, not to transactions in server threads.

subject: springboot
question: In Spring Boot 3, how does /actuator/env show property values by default?
options: Values are shown in plain text
All values are masked
Only passwords are masked
Values are hidden only in the prod profile
explanation: Boot 3 changed show-values to never by default, so values are masked unless configured otherwise.

subject: springboot
question: How does Propagation.NESTED differ from REQUIRES_NEW?
options: NESTED creates a new database connection, REQUIRES_NEW does not
NESTED uses a savepoint in the same physical transaction, REQUIRES_NEW starts a separate one
NESTED ignores rollback, REQUIRES_NEW does not
They are identical aliases
explanation: Rolling back a nested scope returns to the savepoint, but an outer rollback also undoes the nested work.

subject: springboot
question: Which Spring Boot utility is designed for testing an auto-configuration's conditions without starting the full application?
options: SpringApplicationBuilder
ApplicationContextRunner
MockMvcBuilders
AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext
explanation: ApplicationContextRunner lets you add configurations and properties and assert on the resulting context quickly.

subject: springboot
question: Why can an @Async method lose the authenticated user from SecurityContextHolder?
options: @Async clears the HTTP session
Security contexts expire after one second
The default strategy is ThreadLocal, so the new thread has no context unless it is propagated
Async methods run as an anonymous system user by design
explanation: Use DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor or a propagating strategy to carry the context to other threads.

subject: springboot
question: A singleton bean receives a prototype bean through its constructor. What does it get each time it uses that field?
options: The same prototype instance, created once at injection time
A proxy that creates a new instance per call by default
null after the first use
A fresh prototype instance on every method call
explanation: Injection happens once; use ObjectProvider, @Lookup or a scoped proxy to get a new prototype each time.

subject: springboot
question: Why is @ConditionalOnMissingBean reliable in auto-configurations but risky in ordinary user @Configuration classes?
options: It is evaluated against beans registered so far, and auto-configurations are processed after user configuration
User configuration classes ignore all conditions
It is evaluated lazily at first injection only in auto-configurations
Auto-configurations are processed in a separate child context
explanation: Condition evaluation depends on registration order; auto-configurations run after user beans are defined, so they see them.

subject: springboot
question: Why can't you switch @Profile-based beans at runtime in a Spring Boot GraalVM native image?
options: Native images cannot read environment variables
Profiles are only supported in WAR deployments
GraalVM strips all annotations
AOT processing fixes the bean definitions at build time
explanation: Native images assume a closed world, so profiles and conditions are evaluated during the AOT build.

subject: springboot
question: dev is active. Which wins: application-dev.properties packaged in the jar, or application.properties in ./config next to the jar?
options: The packaged application-dev.properties
Whichever file was modified most recently
The external ./config/application.properties
Neither; Boot fails because of the conflict
explanation: Boot ranks files outside the jar above packaged ones, including packaged profile-specific files.

question: With Spring Boot's auto-configured ObjectMapper, what happens when a JSON request body contains an unknown property?
options: The request is rejected with 415
Deserialization fails with UnrecognizedPropertyException
The property is ignored and deserialization succeeds
The unknown property is stored in a map automatically
